STH_pirate.22.desc_07: The Kazon have always been free to take what we want, and we want your wealth and technology... so hand it over to us or face the consequences.
STH_pirate.22.desc_08: You are being raided by the Pirate Lord [raiding_leader.GetName], surrender your resources or we shall take them by force.
STH_pirate.22.desc_09: You are being raided by the Pirate Lord [raiding_leader.GetName], surrender your resources or we shall take them by force.
STH_pirate.22.name: Raiders Detected approaching [raiding_target_planet.GetName]
STH_pirate.23.desc:
We have word back from our raiding force, their targets were too scared to face the force of their weapons and waved the white flag in surrender. 

We have taken their resources and wealth... now we celebrate.
STH_pirate.23.name: Raid Target Surrenders
STH_pirate.24.desc: Our raiding party has met a foe that is willing to fight to protect their wealth, our privateers shall now battle and teach them a lesson.
STH_pirate.24.name: Raid Target willing to fight
STH_pirate.25.desc: Our refusal to back down from the threat posed by the raiding party has led to an attack on the planet [raiding_target_planet.GetName]. should the raiding fleet reach the planet they will begin to plunder resources. We must muster a defense and prevent these raiders from taking our resources.
STH_pirate.25.name: System under raiding attack
STH_pirate.28.desc: We were unable to prevent the raiders from pillaging [raiding_target_planet.GetName], the Raiders have made off with a great deal of valuable resources and disappeared into warp, leaving chaos and destruction in their wake.
STH_pirate.28.e: We must not let this happen again.
STH_pirate.28.name: [raiding_target_planet.GetName] Raided!
STH_pirate.29.desc:
Our raiding party has successfully bypassed the would-be defenses standing in their way and returned to us with riches galore! 

It is time for the captains to divide up the rewards and celebrate with their crews.
STH_pirate.29.name: Raid Successful
STH_pirate.3.a: It is our duty to rescue those in trouble.
STH_pirate.3.b: Raise shields we must defend the ship.
STH_pirate.3.desc: [gorn_pirate_rescue_leader.GetName] in command of [gorn_pirate_rescue_ship.GetName] have arrived on the scene. The transport ship is adrift with its power levels failing fast, sensors are picking up faint life signs. The attackers are not currently in the vicinity, but all the signs point towards a trap, in order to rescue the survivors we must lower our shields, but this will almost certainly provoke a large attack against the [gorn_pirate_rescue_ship.GetName].
STH_pirate.3.name: Transport under attack
STH_pirate.30.desc:
Our forces have successfully destroyed the Raiders threatening our planet. 

We have managed to retrieve part of the privateer's cargo, which has been taken from another faction. We can return it or keep it for ourselves.
STH_pirate.30.name: Raiding Force Defeated
STH_pirate.31.a: You win some, you lose some.
STH_pirate.31.desc:
Our raiding fleet has been destroyed without achieving their goal of pirating and plundering. 

We shall soon see if our target now turns and seeks revenge on us.
STH_pirate.31.name: Raiding Force Defeated
STH_pirate.4.desc_01:
We cannot allow innocents to go without rescue, lowering the shields in an attempt to beam as many crew members from the damaged transport as possible. 

Sensors quickly pick up the ambush as it occurs, the attackers clearly waited for the shields to be lowered and launch a full scale assault against our ships.
STH_pirate.4.desc_02:
Despite the transport crew being in danger of their life support failing, the Admiral cannot risk the lives of their own crew. 

Sensors quickly pick up the ambush as it occurs, the attackers obviously grew impatient with waiting and have sent a smaller number of ships to engage our fleet.
STH_pirate.4.name: Pirates Attack!
STH_pirate.5.desc: Our failure to come to the aid of the transport has resulted in the pirates destroying the ship with the loss of all hands.
STH_pirate.5.name: Transport Destroyed
STH_pirate.6.c: Ensure the survivors are treated with care.
STH_pirate.6.desc_01:
Despite the fearsome attack our fleet was able to repel the attack and defeat the raiders. 

Unfortunately there was no indicuation of who the raiders were or what their intentions towards our transport. However the surviors describe snarling and hissing noises and report that several members of the crew were forcibly remove from the ship.
STH_pirate.6.desc_02:
Despite the fearsome attack our fleet was able to repel the attack and defeat the raiders. 

Unfortunately there was no indicuation of who the raiders were or what their intentions towards our transport. It is unfortunate that we were unable to safe the crew.
STH_pirate.6.name: Pirate raiders defeated in battle
STH_policy.10.desc_01:
The [Root.GetName] has always played a pivotal role on the galactic stage and when we speak with a powerful voice, other lesser empires must listen or face the consequences. 

Through the Galactic Forum we may reach out to our neighbours and make them listen to our views.
STH_policy.10.desc_02:
Our role on the galactic stage has always been to promote unity and freedom and ensure the whole galaxy experiences the peace and freedoms that we experience within [Root.GetName]. 

Through the Galactic Forums the empires of the Milky Way come together to negotiate and attempt to shape the galaxy with words and not torpedoes.
STH_policy.10.desc_03:
Our place in the galaxy has always been important, and every decision we should take must prove profitable for us. 

Our investment in the Galactic Forum will provide us with a seat at the galactic table where we can ensure that events work out in the best interest of the [Root.GetName].
STH_policy.10.desc_04:
Our ascension to a place of Galactic power has put us in a strong position to relay the word of our Gods and help others to see the way forward. 

The Galactic Forum will allow us to influence and preach our position to the wider community.
STH_policy.10.name: Galactic Politics
STH_policy.20.desc: Conflict creates instability and this ripples across the Quadrant threatening the peace that we have deemed important to our future plans. Our admiralty has prepared a list of ongoing wars in the known galaxy, presenting us with the choice on which to focus the [Root.GetName]'s diplomatic attention upon.
STH_policy.20.name: Condemn a War
STH_policy.21.desc:
Our Intelligence services and Admirals have prepared a dossier covering the [From.GetName] - [FromFrom.GetName] war, with details on the origins, casualties and potential outcomes of the ongoing war. 

Giving us a number of potential options.
STH_policy.21.name: Condemn a War
STH_policy.22.a: What business is it of theirs?
STH_policy.22.desc: The [From.GetName] has issued a condemnation of our conflict with the [FromFrom.GetName] to the wider galactic community, calling on us to negotiate a peace settlement with the enemy.
STH_policy.22.name: War Condemnation
STH_policy.23.desc: The [From.GetName] has issued a condemnation of the [FromFrom.GetName] and their conflict against us to the wider galactic community, calling for a swift end to the [FromFrom.GetSpeciesAdj] aggression.
STH_policy.23.name: War Support
STH_policy.25.desc:
Our diplomatic service has identified a number of Empires that harbor a negative view of us, one that has deteriorated steadily over the last couple of years. 

The recommendation is to invite them to a conference and attempt to smooth over any ill feeling between our two nations.
STH_policy.25.name: Improve Relations
STH_policy.26.desc: We have received a communique from [Prev.GetName] they wish to invite us to a diplomatic conference in a bid to repair the deteriorating relationship between our two empires.
STH_policy.26.name: Inbound Communications
STH_policy.27.desc: Dear [Root.GetRulerTitle] [Root.GetRulerName] we acknowledge that the relationship between our worlds has reached a low point and we welcome this chance to mend this relationship. The planet [poorRelationPlanet.GetName] would make an ideal location to host this conference.
STH_policy.27.name: Improve Relations
STH_policy.28.desc: [Root.GetRulerTitle] [Root.GetRulerName], we see no need to change the current relationship between our worlds and suggest you focus your attention elsewhere, should you run the risk of further provoking our annoyance.
STH_policy.28.name: Improve Relations
STH_policy.30.desc:
[Root.GetRulerTitle] I am pleased to report that the conference between our world and [poorRelationEvent.GetName] has been a success, with both sides making positive strides towards improving communications and trust. 

Whilst there maybe some ways to go before the relationship can be considered friendly, this is a significant step forward in our relations.
STH_policy.30.name: Update from Conference
STH_policy.31.desc: [Root.GetRulerTitle] I regret to inform you that the conference between our world and [poorRelationEvent.GetName] has been not been the success we had hoped for. The gulf between our two worlds could not be bridged during the Conference and has potentially widened further.
STH_policy.31.name: Update from Conference
STH_policy.33.desc: Over the years we have managed to create rivalries and whilst we have nothing to fear from these empires our diplomatic services are urging us to put some of this bad blood behind us and look to put an end to these ongoing rivalries.
STH_policy.33.name: Rivals
STH_policy.34.desc: We have been approached by [Prev.GetName] who are looking to call us into a diplomatic conference to discuss our ongoing rivalry in a bid to put aside our past differences and build a better future.
STH_policy.34.name: Incoming Communications
STH_policy.35.b: We no longer support this meeting.
STH_policy.35.desc: Greetings [Root.GetRulerTitle] [Root.GetRulerName], we are willing to accept your offer to meet and discuss our ongoing hostilities, we agree to your location on [poorRivalPlanet.GetName] and will send an envoy to meet with your delegation.
STH_policy.35.name: Diplomatic Response
STH_policy.36.desc:
Attention [Root.GetRulerTitle] [Root.GetRulerName], we have heard your plea to meet with us to end our ongoing rivalry. 

Consider your offer refused, we see no need to change the nature of our relationship. 

Be pleased that we do not worsen the relationship.
STH_policy.36.name: Diplomatic Rejection
STH_policy.38.desc: Sirs, we can report back that our diplomatic team has just exited from their meeting with our rivals with positive news, both sides have agreed to put aside past issues and look to forge a better future.
STH_policy.38.name: Diplomatic Conference Concluded
STH_policy.39.desc: Our rivals have stormed away from the conference in fury it appears the conference has not ended well and the relationship has gotten worse!
STH_policy.39.name: Diplomatic Conference Concluded
STH_policy.40.desc: When war spreads out across the Quadrant it threatens every world, the lives of countless, the safety of our allies, and the security of our own borders. Whatever reason most compels us to act we have a chance to use our power and influence to attempt to end an ongoing war.
STH_policy.40.name: Peacekeeping
STH_policy.41.a: We have no choice but to accept.
STH_policy.41.desc: [Root.GetRulerTitle], your war is unjust and your continued assaults against the innocent must not continue, we urge you to cease this campaign, should you not take this friendly advice you may find that you are forced to under the firepower of our starships.
STH_policy.41.name: End the War!
STH_policy.42.b: They must pay for what they have done.
STH_policy.42.desc: The ongoing [Root.From.GetName] cannot continue, the cost of the war is too high and spreads out across worlds outside of your own. We have convinced [Root.From.attacker.GetName] to lay down their weapons, we now ask that you put your weapons aside and end this conflict.
STH_policy.42.name: End the War!
STH_policy.43.b: We join the war against them.
STH_policy.43.desc: Unfortunately, [From.Attacker.GetName] has not responded well to our demand to call a ceasefire and the bloodshed is set to continue.
STH_policy.43.name: No Ceasefire
STH_policy.44.desc:
Despite calls for a ceasefire in the ongoing conflict, it appears that neither side is prepared to stand down and negotiate a ceasefire. 

The War rages on.
STH_policy.44.name: No Ceasefire
STH_policy.45.desc:
Thanks to the timely intervention by an outside party the ongoing [From.GetName] has arrived at a ceasefire, with all parties withdrawing their forces back behind their borders and powering down their weapons. 

Only time will tell how long this will last, but many are calling for the opportunity to give peace a chance.
STH_policy.45.name: Ceasefire Comes into Effect
STH_policy.46.desc: A ceasefire has been called to end the current hostilities between on worlds involved in the [FromFrom.GetName] conflict. All vessels must return to their own territory immediately.
STH_policy.46.name: Ceasefire in place
STH_policy.47.desc: Despite the best efforts of our ambassadors and envoys, they were unable to persuade [From.Defender.GetName] to abandon the war, it is regretable that peace was so close, yet could not be achieved on this occassion.
STH_policy.47.name: War will continue
STH_policy.48.desc:
Following a failed attempt to end the war, the negotiating party has joined the war on the side of the defenders. 

This could prove to turn the war in their favour, only time will tell.
STH_policy.48.name: The War continues
STH_policy.50.desc:
Our ongoing [playerWar.GetName] continues to cost lives, ships, planets and resources with no end in sight. 

Our diplomats urge us to reach out to our neighbours and request they join us in defeating our enemies.
STH_policy.50.name: War Support
STH_policy.51.a: We shall join you in battle.
STH_policy.51.desc: Greetings [Root.GetRulerTitle] [Root.GetRulerName], we are willing to accept your offer to meet and discuss our ongoing hostilities, we agree to your location on [poorRivalPlanet.GetName] and will send an envoy to meet with your delegation.
STH_policy.51.name: War Support
STH_policy.52.desc: We regret to inform you that we cannot aid you in your ongoing wars, this is a battle you must win on your own. To drag us into your struggles is to put our own borders at risk, and that is not something we can afford right now.
STH_policy.52.name: War Support Rejected
STH_policy.53.desc: We hear your call for aid and the armies of [Root.GetName] will fly to your aid and together we shall be victorious!
STH_policy.53.name: War Support Accepted
STH_policy.54.desc: It appears our war enemy has decided that they cannot defeat us by themselves and have enlisted the help of [fromfromfrom.GetName] in a bid to defeat our forces.
STH_policy.54.name: New Party joins the war!
STH_policy.60.desc: We should establish a truce with one of our powerful and dangerous neighbours to secure our borders and prevent an attack. By reaching out to their envoys we can ask if they will be open to peace talks.
STH_policy.60.name: Establish a Truce
STH_policy.61.desc: We have been approached by [Prev.GetName] who are looking to call us into a diplomatic peace conference to discuss establishing a truce between our empires and the start of peace between our worlds.
STH_policy.61.name: Establish a Truce
STH_policy.62.desc: Greetings [Root.GetRulerTitle] [Root.GetRulerName], we are here to inform you that the people of [from.GetName] have no interest in your offer of peace and a truce. We would welcome the chance to challenge you in combat should it come to this.
STH_policy.62.name: Truce has been rejected
STH_policy.63.desc: Greetings [Root.GetRulerTitle] [Root.GetRulerName], we have listened to your offer and are open to further discussions on the topic of a short-term truce. We have opened our borders and will host an envoy at our capital to further discuss this proposal.
STH_policy.63.name: Open to peace talks
STH_policy.64.desc: We have listened to your representatives and we agree that peace is in the best interest of both our worlds at this point in time and we will sign a short-term truce and ensure that no hostilities erupt between our forces whilst this truce is in effect.
STH_policy.64.name: Truce Established
STH_policy.65.desc: We have listened to your representatives and we do not agree that peace is in the best interest of both our worlds at this point in time. This proposal is too restrictive and we are not inclined to offer you assurances that our forces will not defeat you in combat.
STH_policy.65.name: Truce Rejected
STH_policy.80.desc: Greetings, this is where you can manage the ongoing expeditions and multi-year missions that are currently in progress.
STH_policy.80.name: Expedition Menu
STH_policy.81.a.response: There are no fleets involved in the expedition.
STH_policy.81.a: How many fleets are currently involved in the expedition?
STH_policy.81.b.response: There is 1 fleet engaged in the expedition - the [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_1.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_2.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_3.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_4.GetName] & [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_5.GetName].
STH_policy.81.c.response: There are 2 fleets engaged in the expedition - the [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_1.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_2.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_3.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_4.GetName] & [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_5.GetName].
STH_policy.81.d.response: There are 3 fleets engaged in the expedition - the [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_1.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_2.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_3.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_4.GetName] & [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_5.GetName].
STH_policy.81.desc: Greetings sir, please find a summary of the ongoing activity within our expedition to the Lembatta Cluster, allowing you to add extra ships, remove ships or recall and end the expedition.
STH_policy.81.e.response: There are 5 fleets engaged in the expedition - the [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_1.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_2.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_3.GetName], [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_4.GetName] & [expedition_lembatta_star_cluster_fleet_5.GetName].
STH_policy.81.h: Send another fleet to the Cluster.
STH_policy.81.name: Manage Lembatta Cluster Expedition
STH_policy.90.desc: This taskforce is dedicated to checking for Assimilated Pops Groups within our borders, use this screen to run an ad hoc check across our population.
STH_policy.90.name: Assimilated Pops
STH_policy.999.deassim.tooltip: Check and manage any assimilated pops within your empire.
STH_policy.999.desc:
Welcome to the Advance Diplomacy Menu, from here you can interact with your agencies, and special contacts and engage in the galactic policy options from a single screen. 

As you establish new agencies or special vassals they will be added to this menu.
STH_policy.999.name: Advance Diplomacy Menu
STH_prodigy.10.desc:
[prodigy_target_country.GetName] we are the Vau N'Akat Order from the world of Solum, a world that returns to take its vengeance and I am the Diviner... Note that we bring you your destruction at the hands of one of your vessels of peace. 

Prepare for the revenge of the Vau N'Akat.
STH_prodigy.10.name: The Protostar arrives
STH_prodigy.100.desc:
Our monitoring stations have picked up the incoming signal of what can only be a vessel equipped with a Proto-Drive, which in this case can only be the missing USS Protostar. 

A local task force fleet was sent to intercept the ship, but we have lost contact, we should send another fleet to investigate.
STH_prodigy.100.name: Proto-Warp Signal Detected
STH_prodigy.101.desc: On board the Protostar Dal and the ETH frantically attempt to shut down the Proto-drive before the ship reaches its destination, knowing that the ship now carries unwanted intruders, looking to attack [Root.GetName].
STH_prodigy.101.name: Supernova
STH_prodigy.102.desc_01:
Rok-Tahk and Murf head toward the Protostar's computer core in an attempt to scrap the core and with it the Living Construct, as the pair reach the core the terrifying sight of a Drednok robotic warrior stands between the pair and their destination. 

 The warrior launches an attack on the pair, Rok-Tahk uses her impressive strength to hold off the Drednok's first attack, but even the Brikarian strength is no match for the war machine. 

Just as Rok-Tahk is about to be defeated, Murf untangles himself and launches themselves at the Drednok with lighting fast speed and agility, driving the Drednok back and away from the computer core... allowing Rok-Tahk to reach the panel, the damage to the control panel was significant. Turning Rok-Tahk joins Murf in facing their robotic foe.
STH_prodigy.102.desc_02:
Rok-Tahk heads toward the Protostar's computer core in an attempt to scrap the core and with it the Living Construct, as she reaches the core the terrifying sight of a Drednok robotic warrior stands between Rok and the computer core control panel. 

 The warrior launches an attack on Rok-Tahk using her impressive strength to hold off the Drednok's first attack just about keeps Rok safe, but the more powerful Drednok begins to overwhelm even the powerful Brikarian, Rok-Tahk knows that the only way to reach the Computer Core is to defeat the robotic warrior.
STH_prodigy.102.name: Supernova
STH_prodigy.103.desc: The Drednok lies crumpled and defeated, overpowered by its attack, allowing Rok-Tahk to reach the computer core's main panel, reaching it they can unlock the mechanism, unfortunately, the Drednok has already been able to prevent the core from being overloaded and destroyed... but at least they can do no further damage.
STH_prodigy.103.name: Drednok Defeated
STH_prodigy.104.desc:
Drednok stands over the still form of Rok-Tahk, the gentle Brikarian no longer moving or able to take any further action to help her friends. 

Drednok moves towards the computer core ready to unleash the Living Construct on the [Root.GetName] Fleet.
STH_prodigy.104.name: Drednok Wins the Battle
STH_prodigy.105.desc: Jankom Pog knows that the Living Construct needs to open communication channels with the other vessels to spread its virus throughout the approaching fleet, if Jankom Pog can disable the Protostar's communication array then the damage could be limited and the number of reinforcements could be reduced significantly.
STH_prodigy.105.name: Supernova
STH_prodigy.106.desc: Jankom Pog clenches his fist in celebration, only an engineer with Jankom Pog's unique skills could have accomplished the task, as the Tellarite looks over the 'disabled' communication relay, the strength of the Vau N'Akat's forces should be depleted as a result.
STH_prodigy.106.name: Jankom Pog to the rescue
STH_prodigy.107.desc: Jankom Pog slams his fist against the comms panel, the signal has already been sent and the message has left the Protostar, despite the Tellarite's efforts Jankom Pog was moments too slow.
STH_prodigy.107.name: Jankom Pog Defeated
STH_prodigy.108.desc: On the Bridge of the USS Protostar Zero hears the thoughts in Dal's head before he vocalizes it, the only way to prevent the Construct Virus from spreading is to destroy the Protostar and everyone onboard. An idea springs into Zero's mind, the Protostar need not be destroyed if Zero can trigger an electromagnetic surge to shut down all of the Protostar's systems in a single event.
STH_prodigy.108.name: Supernova
STH_prodigy.109.desc:
Zero manages to generate a large EMP burst using the local sun's solar flares, as the lights onboard the Protostar go dark, rapidly followed by all the consoles throughout the ship. 

The Protostar is out of the fight, but the Construct Virus can cause no further harm to nearby fleet.
STH_prodigy.109.name: Zero Successful
STH_prodigy.11.desc: As the Vau N'Akat's plans begin to come into effect as they declare war against us, the Construct's virus begins to take effect on a number of our ships, with their systems quickly succumbing and the vessels joining the Vau N'Akat's fleets against us.
STH_prodigy.11.name: Fleets compromised by the Construct
STH_prodigy.110.desc:
The attempt to disable the Protostar was unsuccessful, the EMP burst was just not powerful enough to overcome the Protostar's shielding. 

With no choice left Dal sets the auto-destruct and orders a full evacuation of their ship and home.
STH_prodigy.110.name: Zero Unsuccessful.
STH_prodigy.111.desc: Gwyn can sense her father's presence onboard the Protostar as he stalks Dal on the bridge, Gwyn leaps forward and uses her heirloom to deflect the Diviner's attack against her friend. The two warriors begin to battle, Gwyn fully aware that should she lose nothing will be able to stop the Diviner and the Order's plans for revenge.
STH_prodigy.111.name: Supernova
STH_prodigy.112.desc: After a furious battle between father and his progeny, the Diviner lies wounded and defeated. Reaching out to Gwyn the Diviner lays down his weapon and surrenders .
STH_prodigy.112.name: The Diviner Defeated
STH_prodigy.113.desc: Gwyn collapses to the floor, mortally wounded by her father blade, as the Diviner cries out in shock and horror, unable to contemplate what he has done to his progeny.
STH_prodigy.113.name: The Diviner Victorious
STH_prodigy.114.desc_01:
[prodigy_hero_leader.GetName] wakes up onboard the Protostar's sickbay, unsure of how long they have been unconscious they head towards the ship's bridge. 

On reaching the command deck [prodigy_hero_leader.GetName] notices a Vau N'Akat general lying prone on the floor, but crucially an open communication back to Solum urging the rest of the fleet to join the battle and open up a wormhole right into the heart of [Root.GetName] space. This could be the last chance to appeal to the Vau N'Akat to abandon their plans for revenge.
STH_prodigy.114.desc_02:
[prodigy_hero_leader.GetName] wakes up onboard the Protostar's sickbay, unsure of how long they have been unconscious they head towards the ship's bridge. 

On reaching the command deck [prodigy_hero_leader.GetName] they are attacked by the Diviner, who appeared to have been trying to open a Wormhole back to Solum via the same anomaly in the Proto-Drive that started this adventure. 

If the Captain can reach the panel they might be able to convince the Vau N'Akat that [Root.GetName] does not threaten them.
STH_prodigy.114.name: Supernova
STH_prodigy.115.desc: Using all their skills the Starfleet officer manages to reach the Vau N'Akat Order, using an impassioned speech, the Vau N'Akat Order agree that now is not the time for further escalation of the ongoing conflict and agree that for now, they will leave the Diviner to his plans.
STH_prodigy.115.name: Escalation Avoided
STH_prodigy.116.desc: The situation only escalates, the Order members are not convinced by [Root.GetName]'s efforts and their resolve to join the Diviner in Battle has only hardened.
STH_prodigy.116.name: Situation Escalates
STH_prodigy.117.desc_01:
With all the efforts completed the fate of the mission now lands with Dal, his crew have done all they can to buy Dal enough time to get the Protostar and its dangerous Construct Virus away from the fleet and away from causing more harm. 

With the ship in a critical state it will take all of Dal's skills and abilities as a pilot and captain!
STH_prodigy.117.desc_02:
With all the efforts completed the fate of the mission now lands with Dal, his crew have done all they can to buy Dal enough time to get the Protostar and its dangerous Construct Virus away from the fleet and away from causing more harm. 

With the ship in a critical state it will take all of Dal's skills and abilities as a pilot and captain, but first Dal must get passed the Diviner who now stands in his way.
STH_prodigy.117.name: Supernova Part II
STH_prodigy.118.a: The fleets are on a collision course.
STH_prodigy.118.desc_01: Dal manages to get the Protostar clear of the oncoming fleet and prevents any further [Root.GetName] ships from being consumed by the Construct Virus. Just as all seems ok, the original fleet that was investigating the Proto-Drive signal appears from behind a nearby asteroid, their crews have no control over their ships they have been fully taken over by the Construct Virus and belong to the Diviner and his minions!
STH_prodigy.118.desc_02:
The Protostar is simply too damaged and disabled for Dal to successfully move it and the scout ship now drifts dangerously in the path of the oncoming fleet still broadcasting the deadly virus. 

To make matters worse the original fleet which was investigating the Proto-Drive signal appears from behind a nearby asteroid, their crews have no control over their ships they have been fully taken over by the Construct Virus and belong to the Diviner and his minions!
STH_prodigy.118.name: Supernova Part II
STH_prodigy.119.desc_01:
As Dal guides the Protostar clear of the battle zone, knowing that at least the outbound communications from the Protostar will not be able to impact any of the inbound ships. 

The compromised fleet begins to power up its weapons ready to target the new fleet.
STH_prodigy.119.desc_02:
As the Protostar begins its final auto-destruct sequence the young crew climbs into the escape pods, at least the destruction of their ship will help safeguard the lives on the ships heading towards them. 

The compromised fleet begins to power up its weapons ready to target the new fleet.
STH_prodigy.119.desc_03:
As the Protostar limps away from the battle site, its comm channel still broadcasting the Living Constructs dangerous virus, Dal can only hope that the damage will be limited by the distance the Protostar has now traveled from the battlezone.

 On the viewscreen he can see the compromised fleet begins to power up its weapons ready to target the new fleet.
STH_prodigy.119.desc_04:
Failure to prevent the communications from leaving the Protostar risks infecting further ships with the Constructs Virus, but the untimely destruction of the Protostar might at the very least restrict the impact of the Living Construct. 

The compromised fleet begins to power up its weapons ready to target the new fleet.
STH_prodigy.119.name: Supernova Part II
STH_prodigy.12.desc: As the Construct's effect makes its way through the fleet, our engineers propose a solution that involves cutting all intra-ship communications. to halt the spread of the Construct virus, at the short-term effect of our battle effectiveness.
STH_prodigy.12.name: Ships fall prey to the Construct
STH_prodigy.121.desc: With the battle over Dal watches as the remaining [Root.GetName] ships begin their search for the Protostar in a bid to try and salvage the ship and rescue what remains of his young crew.
STH_prodigy.121.name: The Protostar is safe
STH_prodigy.122.desc: With the battle over Dal watches as the remaining [Root.GetName] ships begin their search for the young crew of the Protostar in their escape pods.
STH_prodigy.122.name: The Protostar has been destroyed
STH_prodigy.123.desc: As the debris floats over the site of the battle, A message echoes across subspace, Solum will be avenged for the crimes the [Root.GetName] will commit against our people... the Diviner may have been defeated but the Vau N'Akat Order has been awakened and are coming for you.
STH_prodigy.123.name: Harsh Words from Solum
STH_prodigy.124.desc:
As feared following the attack by the Diviner, the Vau N'Akat are declaring war on us for a perceived attack that they believe we would have committed in the future. 

The tunnel that was opened by the Protostar has been stabilised and now offers a route between our worlds and a way fot them to attack us.
STH_prodigy.124.name: War with the Vau N'Akat
STH_prodigy.125.desc: As the preverbal dust settles in the aftermath of the Diviners attack on our fleets, a message comes in from Solum, it appears our Captain's message of peace has, for now, reached calmer ears. The Order appears to be content to leave us in peace for the moment.
STH_prodigy.125.name: A message of Peace from Solum
STH_prodigy.127.desc: Greetings all, I am [tempLeader] and I wanted to thank you for your efforts in resolving the Protostar crisis and time to reward these young leaders with a pace amongst our ranks.
STH_prodigy.127.name: Prodigy
STH_prodigy.2.desc:
We have received an emergency message from the USS Protostar, which had to abandon the test of its proto-warp jump. It appears an instability in the protostar drive almost generated a temporal incursion, resulting in an emergency shutdown. 

Results of the test have been fed back to Starfleet who will roll out the fix to all ships of this class within the fleet.
STH_prodigy.2.name: USS Protostar Survives Proto-Warp jump
STH_prodigy.20.desc:
On the remote slave-mining asteroid of Tars Lamora, the cruel overlord known only as The Diviner holds sway over his prisoners and slaves, using them to dig for a treasure greater than minerals. 

Amongst all the slaves one young adventurer, named Dal R'El makes an amazing discovery... an abandoned Starship.
STH_prodigy.20.name: Lost and Found
STH_prodigy.21.a.response: Once I have my prize, your miserable lives are worthless.
STH_prodigy.21.a: If I do this can I go free?
STH_prodigy.21.b.response: The salvation of my people, the revenge for a generation lost... my Protostar!
STH_prodigy.21.c.response: Isn't it obvious? If you try to escape, she will kill you.
STH_prodigy.21.c: Why are you asking me to take Gwyn?
STH_prodigy.21.d: Go with Gwyn, escape will come later.
STH_prodigy.21.desc: Dal R'El, you stand before your Diviner and his progeny, my Gwyndala - my daughter. We are aware of your find within our mines and I demand that you take my Gwyn to its location. Failure to do as I command will see not only a punishment for yourself, but for your fellow prisoners.
STH_prodigy.21.e: Insist on going alone, it will be easier to escape.
STH_prodigy.21.name: Lost and Found
STH_prodigy.22.a: Agree to meet Zero on the ship.
STH_prodigy.22.desc_01:
As Dal and Gwyn make their way down the mine tunnel, a strange voice fills Dal's mind. 

Don't be alarmed my name is Zero, I am a Medusan, and on the run from the Diviner. He would use my appearance as a Medusan to punish those who displeased him, I had no choice but to escape.
STH_prodigy.22.desc_02:
As Dal makes his way down the mine tunnel, a strange voice fills Dal's mind. 

Don't be alarmed my name is Zero, I am a Medusan, and on the run from the Diviner. He would use my appearance as a Medusan to punish those who displeased him, I had no choice but to escape.
STH_prodigy.22.name: Fugitive Zero
STH_prodigy.23.desc_01:
Having agreed to meet Zero on the ship, Dal progresses to be confronted by a towering Brikar and a diminutive Tellarite. 'Jankom Pog here's that you are getting out of here, Jankom Pog can help you!' grunts the Tellarite, the towering Brikar makes a low grumbling nose, which sounds like two boulders colliding. 

Dal laughs, it is clear this escape has taken on a story of its own!
STH_prodigy.23.desc_02:
Dal progresses to be confronted by a towering Brikar and a diminutive Tellarite. 'Jankom Pog here's that you are getting out of here, Jankom Pog can help you!' grunts the Tellarite, the towering Brikar makes a low grumbling nose, which sounds like two boulders colliding. 

Dal laughs, how many more tag-alongs will this escape involve?
STH_prodigy.23.desc_03:
Dal progresses to be confronted by a towering Brikar and a diminutive Tellarite. 'Jankom Pog here's that you are getting out of here, Jankom Pog can help you!' grunts the Tellarite, the towering Brikar makes a low grumbling nose, which sounds like two boulders colliding. 

Dal laughs, it is clear this escape has taken on a story of its own!
STH_prodigy.23.name: Rok-Tahk and Jankom Pog
STH_prodigy.24.desc:
Dal, Jankom & the Brikar, who identify themselves as Rok-Tahk, the moment that they enter the bridge of the strange alien vessel, look around in excitement as interior lighting and control panels come to life. Dal looks around at his new crew, this is our chance to escape he yells. 

The crew looks to Gwyn, the young Vau N'Akat jumps to one of the consoles and powers up the ship's engines. 

It seems like we are in this together.
STH_prodigy.24.name: Lost and Found Part 2
STH_prodigy.25.desc:
Dal and those he gathered reach the bridge of the vessel, which lights up to greet them, the chance to escape before them Dal looks to Gwyn, imploring her to join him. 

The young Vau N'Akat warrior slowly shakes her head and taps her communicator.... 'Father I have the ship'.
STH_prodigy.25.name: Lost and Found Part 2
STH_prodigy.26.desc: Dal and Gwyn arrive on the bridge of the Protostar, which lights up to greet them, the chance to escape before them the pair look at each other, Gwyn looks out the viewport towards the approaching waves of Drednok warriors and calls to Dal, 'I have to escape my Father, I can no longer be apart of his cruel plans'.
STH_prodigy.26.name: Lost and Found Part 2
STH_prodigy.3.desc:
Our long-range scans have picked up the debris from a small starship that appears to have exited Proto-Warp under an emergency, the ship can only be the USS Protostar, which was testing the new drive system. 

There are no signs of any survivors from the ship and all remaining black box information has been passed back to Starfleet Engineering to attempt to prevent a repeat of this tragedy.
STH_prodigy.3.name: USS Protostar Destroyed
STH_prodigy.30.desc:
The Protostar saws clear of Tars Lamora, its powerful phasers clearing the Diviner's battle units from its path, as the crew cheered and celebrated, the Diviner looked on with an angry look. 

Back on the Protostar Dal takes the centre seat and the adventure begins.
STH_prodigy.30.name: Prodigy Begins!
STH_prodigy.31.desc:
The Protostar attempts to clear the surface of Tars Lamora, but the Diviner's forces swarm the ship, working their way through the hull and into the vital systems of the ship. 

As Dal orders the ship to engage its powerful engineers a crucial system fails and a fatal cascade begins which ends with a catastrophic explosion that engulfs and destroys the Protostar, ending its journey early.
STH_prodigy.31.name: Prodigy Ends!
STH_prodigy.4.desc:
In concerning news, the USS Protostar has vanished while undertaking its first Proto-warp jump, our long-range scans cannot find any evidence of debris or signs from the Protostar's small crew. 

We can however see signs of a small temporal anomaly that appeared briefly following the disappearance of the ship.
STH_prodigy.4.name: USS Protostar vanishes in Protowarp Flight
STH_prodigy.40.desc: Six young heroes, former detainees at a mining colony overseen by the mysterious Diviner, discoverered the derelict Starfleet ship, the USS Protostar, hidden within the asteroid. This inexperienced crew launches a harrowing getaway aboard the starship. Together the escapees learn that the ship came from a far-off alliance of peaceful galactic explorers known as the Federation. They resolve to set a course for Starfleet, but the Diviner is hot on their trails. Their journey takes them on a wild adventure where they encounter strange new life and civilizations, learn about Starfleet's ideals, and hope to find a better future for themselves on the far side of the galaxy.
STH_prodigy.40.name: Prodigy Begins!
STH_prodigy.41.desc: The crew hear a strange noise emanating from the back of the bridge, on investigating they find a small, but friendly gelatinous being who calls himself Murf!
STH_prodigy.41.name: Murf
STH_prodigy.45.desc: As the Protostar exits a period of Proto-Warp with the drive requiring an extended period of cooldown, the crew finds themselves with some downtime. Exploring the ship Dal finds a holodeck and an interesting holodeck program named the Kobayashi Maru scenario - a test of a captains leadership skills.
STH_prodigy.45.name: Kobayashi
STH_prodigy.46.desc: The holographic simulation loads up placing Dal and the centre of a Starship bridge, with an incoming hail from a freighter in danger. Arriving at the scene the freighter is quickly attacked and destroyed by a fleet of Warbirds ending the simulation with the dreaded phrase.
STH_prodigy.46.name: Kobayashi
STH_prodigy.47.b: A no win scenario must be the point!
STH_prodigy.47.desc: As the number of attempts racks up, Dal's frustration levels only increase, at what point does this simulation become an unwinnable scenario? Is this what the simulations is trying to tell him or is the thing broken?
STH_prodigy.47.name: Kobayashi, 42 attempts later!
STH_prodigy.5.desc: Emerging from a wormhole, torn through space by the Protostar's malfunctioning drive core, the powerless ship comes crashing down on the distant planet of Solum in the Delta Quadrant.
STH_prodigy.5.name: Protostar crashes on Solum
STH_prodigy.50.a: The vines begin to follow the Runaway.
STH_prodigy.50.desc: Landing on a planet named Murder World, the crew begins to investigate their surroundings and collect samples from the local fauna. Gwyn who has been questioning her decision to abandon her father and side with the crew of the Protostar takes a small land vehicle named the 'Runaway' for a drive to clear her mind.
STH_prodigy.50.name: Dream Catcher
STH_prodigy.51.desc:
Gwyn picks up a series of messages from the rest of the crew, it appears the whole planet is one giant superorganism, racing back to the crew she finds Dal and Murf bound by thick red vines. Grabbing her heirloom and rushing forward, Gwyn is stopped by a familiar voice... her father! 

The Diviner calls out concerned for Gwyn's safety, 'come with me my Gwyndala' he pleads...
STH_prodigy.51.name: Dream Catcher
STH_prodigy.52.desc: Emergency Training Hologram's log, It has been almost a week since the cadets on this ship departed to explore the planet, and now I can no longer read their life signs, I can only assume they have been killed in the line of duty. With no hope of rescue, I am powering down the Protostar I can only hope one day this ship is found on this remote world and I can tell the story of these brave cadets.
STH_prodigy.52.name: Crew of the USS Protostar Lost
STH_prodigy.53.desc: Father... it cannot be you, what are you doing here? Shaking her head to try and clear the image of her father from her mind, the Diviner would never be this concerned about her wellbeing, unless he has changed?
STH_prodigy.53.name: Dream Catcher
STH_prodigy.54.desc: With the image of the Diviner cleared from her mind, Gwyn races towards Dal and the rest of the crew struggling for their lives. Using her heirloom to free the others, the crew race back to the Protostar and escape from this nightmare world.
STH_prodigy.54.name: Dream Catcher
STH_prodigy.55.desc: With Gwyn's loyalty to the crew of the Protostar secured and the crew safely rescued from Murder World, the Protostar once again sets course for Federation space.
STH_prodigy.55.name: Dream Catcher
STH_prodigy.6.a.response: The Construct is a powerful weapon that will turn your own fleets against you.
STH_prodigy.6.a: What is this Construct you mention?
STH_prodigy.6.b.response: One of your vessels arrived over our planet years ago, sparking a civil war that decimated Solum. no doubt part of your plans to weaken us ahead of a full scale invasion.
STH_prodigy.6.b: What did we ever do to you?
STH_prodigy.6.desc:
Starfleet, I am [vau_nakat_order_leader.GetName] of the Vau N'Akat, we see that you have returned to finish off what you started so many years ago! The civil war that you started nearly destroyed our world, but we prepared for your return and to inflict our revenge upon you and your [prodigy_target_country.GetName]. 

Captain [prodigy_hero_leader.GetName] you and your crew are now our prisoners and your vessel will become home to our 'Construct' a powerful weapon that will turn your ships against you as we wipe your people from the galaxy.
STH_prodigy.6.name: Message from the Vau N'Akat
STH_prodigy.60.desc:
All is not well on the USS Protostar, as the crew discovers the living Construct hidden within the computer core, Rok-Tahk and Murf were exploring the lower levels of the ship when they came across the Construct, a weapon hidden within the ship providing their salvation that could destroy those they were seeking to flee to. 

The thoughts and concerns of the crew were interrupted by the incoming presence of a massive Tachyon storm.
STH_prodigy.60.name: Time Amok
STH_prodigy.61.desc:
As the crew begins preparations, Rok-Tahk reflects her role within the team, for so long she has been seen as the 'muscle' appreciated only for her size and strength and not her mind. 

Suddenly there is a warning from the Proto-Core that something within the storm has set off a major failure within the drive with an explosion imminent. 

As the storm hits the core explodes and the ship explodes...
STH_prodigy.61.name: Time Amok
STH_prodigy.62.a: Coordination across time zones is the only option.
STH_prodigy.62.desc:
The crew find themselves split across timezones with time itself splintered and fractured moving at differing rates across each section of the ship. Some meer seconds away from the core breach, others with time moving so slowly that seconds seem like hours. 

The command training hologram appears to be the only one immune from the effects, as she moves across the sections of the fractured vessel. 

Building a new warp matrix to repair the damaged one might be the only hope the ship has.
STH_prodigy.62.name: Time Amok
STH_prodigy.63.desc:
As each member of the crew does their part it is left to Rok-Tahk whose section moves the slowest to complete the build. As time moves very slowly in this phase, a lonely Rok tries to reconnect to her absent friends by bidding their empty bunks good night when she goes to sleep each 'night' and hugging a small toy representation of Murf. 

Rok-Tahk channels her inner cadet to complete the build, knowing that once complete she has a long time to wait alone by herself.
STH_prodigy.63.name: Time Amok
STH_prodigy.64.desc: An anti-matter warp core breach leaves very little in its wake, but this pales in comparison to the detention of a Proto-core drive, which atomises the ship and all aboard in the blink of an eye.
STH_prodigy.64.name: Protostar Destroyed
STH_prodigy.65.desc_01: Once the device is connected to the proto-drive, the timeline, and the rest of the crew, are restored, alive and well, and recalling they had each died in their time zones. Rok and the ETH meet up with the others gathered on the bridge and with Rok wiping away tears of happiness receives a group hug from the others, who are proud of her achievements. The hologram looks on with a smile, but then becomes saddened, which Gwyn notices and realizes why, going over to her, she quietly asks the hologram how long the young girl spent alone, to which she utters the phrase, 'too long'. As Rok tells the others about her self-education, Gwyn remarks that Rok may not just have found her friends, but also her calling in life.
STH_prodigy.65.desc_02: Once the device is connected to the proto-drive, the timeline, and the rest of the crew, are restored, alive and well, and recalling they had each died in their time zones. Rok and the ETH meet up with the others gathered on the bridge and with Rok wiping away tears of happiness receives a group hug from the others, who are proud of her achievements. The hologram looks on with a smile, but then becomes saddened, which Dal notices and realizes why, going over to her, she quietly asks the hologram how long the young girl spent alone, to which she utters the phrase, 'too long'. As Rok tells the others about her self-education, Dal remarks that Rok may not just have found her friends, but also her calling in life.
STH_prodigy.65.name: Time Amok
STH_prodigy.66.desc:
After a few days of Murf acting strangely the young crew finds the young alien cocooned in a shell of his own making, clearly undergoing some form of metamorphosis! 

With no one knowing the outcome this could pose a risk to the ship.
STH_prodigy.66.name: Murf's Metamurfphosis
STH_prodigy.67.desc: Murf emerges from the cocoon transformed into a new form, a very capable new life and very grateful and loyal to those who cared for him.
STH_prodigy.67.name: Murf's Metamurfphosis
STH_prodigy.7.desc:
Captain [prodigy_hero_leader.GetName] and their First Officer take their chance to escape knowing that should the USS Protostar return to Earth it would bring about the destruction of [Root.GetName]. 

The duo make it to the ship and forcing their way to a command panel successfully send the Protostar through the still open portal to parts unknown and with it the dangerous weapon hidden onboard.
STH_prodigy.7.name: Protostar Escapes to far off Asteroid
STH_prodigy.70.desc:
The Protostar answers a distress call from Planet 0042692 and the crew are greeted by representatives of the colony of New Enda-Prize. A colony who were visited by the crew of the Enterprise and grew up idolising the ways of 'Those Old Scientists'. 

The colony is suffering from a mysterious plague, from the mysterious Gallows.
STH_prodigy.70.name: All the World's a Stage
STH_prodigy.71.a: Force the shuttle into the Pit.
STH_prodigy.71.desc:
Jankom Pog, the Protostar defacto engineer, was the logical choice to investigate the gallows. On inspection, they find a crashed Type-F shuttlecraft the Galileo leaking warp plasma into the environment. 

Knowing that no one else could repair the damage, Jankom Pog leaps onto the Shuttle. 

With two options availale to Jankom Pog, he can either repair the comms relay, force the shuttle into the pit to seal the leak and beam away, or attempt to fix the plasma leak himself.
STH_prodigy.71.name: All the World's a Stage
STH_prodigy.72.desc:
The Shuttle begins it's final decent into the cavern, and just as Jankom Pog is about to give up hope, the familiar hum of the transporter rings out as Dal and the Enda-Prizians beam him to safety. 

With the colony safe. Jankom Pog having learned a valuable lesson the crew resumes the journey to Federation space.
STH_prodigy.72.name: All the World's a Stage
STH_prodigy.73.desc:
The Shuttle begins it's final descent into the cavern, Jankom Pog looks on and the Shuttlecraft breaks up around him, knowing that once again his sacrifice has saved lives. 

The crew of the Protostar having saved the colony, but lost a member of their family continue their voyage to Federation space.
STH_prodigy.73.name: All the World's a Stage
STH_prodigy.74.desc:
Jankom Pog frantically completes the repairs to Galileo's damaged warp core meer seconds before the core goes critical and dumps its toxic warp plasma into the biosphere of the planet. 

Jankom Pog falls to the floor relieved at having saved the day before the hum of the Protostar's transporter whisks him away and the ship resumes its journey back to Starfleet.
STH_prodigy.74.name: All the World's a Stage
STH_prodigy.75.desc:
Jankom Pog frantically completes the repairs to Galileo's damaged warp core meer seconds before the core goes critical and dumps its toxic warp plasma into the biosphere of the planet. 

Jankom Pog falls to the floor his body shaking from the toxic effects of the warp plasma exposure, knowing the signs of the overdose all too well, the engineer smiles and closes his eyes knowing that at least his sacrifice saved the colony. 

The crew of the Protostar having saved the colony, but lost a member of their family continued their voyage to Federation space.
STH_prodigy.75.name: All the World's a Stage
STH_prodigy.8.desc:
Captain [prodigy_hero_leader.GetName] and their First Officer take their chance to escape knowing that should the USS Protostar return to Earth it would bring about the destruction of [Root.GetName]. 

The duo make it back to where the Protostar was being held. but despite their efforts, they could not remotely free the ship, with no choice remaining the Captain sets the auto-destruct and the pair waits for the inevitable destruction of their ship and with it the weapon that could have caused so much impact.
STH_prodigy.8.name: Protostar Explodes
STH_prodigy.80.desc: As the crew debate options to remove the Living Construct from the Protostar, their scanners detect the presence of a large dormant Cuboid ship, which their Training Hologram identifies as a Borg Cube. Excited by the prospect of using the advanced technology of the Borg to defeat the Construct the crew prepare to board the Borg vessel.
STH_prodigy.80.name: Let Sleeping Borg Lie
STH_prodigy.81.desc:
The crew wonder through the black corridors, feeling with each step that they are being watched by the rows and rows of sleeping drones. 

As a Medusan Zero begins to hear the voice of the collective calling out seeking to know more about the young individuals who may pose a new threat to the collective.
STH_prodigy.81.name: Let Sleeping Borg Lie
STH_prodigy.82.desc: Zero leads the crew to the Borg Vinculum and brief discussion later it is clear that only Zero would be able to withstand the power of the Collective. As dangerous as it would be Zero needs to go into the mind of the Borg and look for the information they need.
STH_prodigy.82.name: Let Sleeping Borg Lie
STH_prodigy.83.desc: Zero and the crew reach the Protostar as the Cube springs back into life, the Borg Cube reaches out with it's tractor beam, but the Protostar is just too quick and leaps into warp before the Borg can react further... But it looks like the young rookies have alerted the Borg to the Federations possession of Proto-Warp and made Starfleet a target.
STH_prodigy.83.name: Let Sleeping Borg Lie
STH_prodigy.84.desc:
Zero and the crew reach the Protostar, but the Borg Cube is already powering up and lashes out with a tractor beam and before the kids can react a dozen Borg Drones beam onto the ship, they say assimilation is painless... they were wrong. 

As the Borg collective add other crew to their collective, Starfleet once again becomes of interest to the Collective.
STH_prodigy.84.name: Let Sleeping Borg Lie
STH_prodigy.85.desc:
The lure of the Collective is all-encompassing, the pull of the hive, the embrace of the many... 

 Resistance is Futile, we are Borg.
STH_prodigy.85.name: The Collective
STH_prodigy.86.desc: We are the Borg, your distinctiveness will join us, become one with us, be part of our hive, our collective, perfection.
STH_prodigy.86.name: The Collective
STH_prodigy.87.desc:
As the crew of the Protostar await for the return of Zero, they receive a communication from the Cube. 

The assimilated form of Zero appears on screen and utters the chilling phrase 'You will be assimilated'. 

As the Borg collective add other crew to their collective, Starfleet once again becomes of interest to the Collective.
STH_prodigy.87.name: Let Sleeping Borg Lie
STH_prodigy.88.desc:
Breaking free of the Collective's hold was difficult but Zero manages it, whilst putting the Collective back into their slumber. 

The Borg may not hold the answers to the Construct, but Zero found an inner strength and belief in themselves.
STH_prodigy.88.name: Let Sleeping Borg Lie
STH_prodigy.9.desc: The Vau N'Akat's plan is quickly put into effect, with the Protostar sent back through the wormhole and sent on a direct course for the very centre of [Root.GetName] carrying the Construct program and its ability to remote hijack friendly vessels and turn them against their former masters.
STH_prodigy.9.name: Protostar sent back to [Root.GetName]
STH_prodigy.90.a: We have to plan a rescue.
STH_prodigy.90.desc:
As the crew of the Protostar nears Federation space, they pick up a distress call originating from the distant world of Solum, from none other than [prodigy_hero_leader.GetName] held captive at the hands of the Vau N'Akat. 

The original Captain of the Protostar is out there asking for help. Should we turn the ship around or abandon them?
STH_prodigy.90.name: Last Flight of the Protostar
STH_prodigy.91.desc: The Protostar exits warp over Solum, and scanning the planet picks up the life signs of [prodigy_hero_leader.GetName], it will take as many of the crew as possible to pull of the rescue.
STH_prodigy.91.name: Last Flight of the Protostar
STH_prodigy.92.a: It's time to bring this adventure to an end.
STH_prodigy.92.desc:
The rescue is complete and a battered and bruised [prodigy_hero_leader.GetName] safely recovering in the Protostar's medical bay, Dal and the Protostar are free to return to Starfleet and warn them of the threat the Vau N'Akat bring. 

However, the threat of the Living Construct must be overcome...

Just as the crew are about to celebrate their success, the Intruder Alert alarm signals, a team from Solum has infiltrated the ship and set the Protostar on a course back to [Root.GetName] space.
STH_prodigy.92.name: Last Flight of the Protostar
STH_prodigy.93.a: It's time to bring this adventure to an end.
STH_prodigy.93.desc:
The crew looks down at the body of [prodigy_hero_leader.GetName] the mission a complete failure, perhaps if the crew was better placed, or more able, but that doesn't matter now, it is time to return to Starfleet and bring the mission to an end. 

Just as the crew are about to calculate their next move, the Intruder Alert alarm signals, a team from Solum has infilatrated the ship and set the Protostar on a course back to [Root.GetName] space.
STH_prodigy.93.name: Last Flight of the Protostar
STH_qless_category_desc: Scans of [ROOT.GetName] show a far greater variability in the gravitational field than would be expected of an asteroid of this size and type. Such readings are normally associated with valuable exotic-matter crystalline deposits.
STH_qpedia.1.a.response: You'll find a collection of important Q-tips... yes the ones you probably muted and selectively written articles on the how to play STNH.
STH_qpedia.1.b.response: Of course! We aim to cover all the unique mechanics.
STH_qpedia.1.b: Can I find articles on specific Empires?
STH_qpedia.1.desc:
Ah, so you have seen sense and have come to your favorite omnipotent being, Uncle Q for help?

Well you are in the right place, I know all there is to know about everything, especially the STNH modiverse. Have a look at the list of questions below, the list will be continuously updated and of course feel free to let the Qs know if something is missing.
STH_qpedia.1.e.response:
Well, well... the human desire to have what is not allowed. You may be aware that there are now certain systems that you may want to own, but are unable to build an outpost in them. 

There are now two new types of systems which you cannot own. The 1st type are environmental systems, such as certain black holes, nebulas, or hazard systems, these are designed to split up the map for gameplay reasons. 

The second type called event systems, are added for event purposes and may serve a story purpose at a later stage.
STH_qpedia.1.f.response:
First Contacts: The Romulans, Klingons, Suliban and other races have access to the Vanilla cloaking mechanic.

Nemesis: The Nemesis DLC adds a few additional base game espionage operations to the game.

Utopia: Advanced slavery options added, included Remans added as battle thralls, unique slavery options for the Orion, Breen.

Synthetic Dawn: Two new races added to the game, the Cravic and the Pralor become playable.

MegaCorp: The Orion & Ferengi are converted to megacorp empires with all the unique associated features.

Apocalypse: Planet Killer ships added to the game for the Undine, Scimitar, Xindi & Krenim.

Federations: Unlocks the federation types included in this DLC. Note this doesn't impact the formation of the UFP.

Aquatics: The Chelarians have been added as a playable race and the Selkie are included as a warp-capable primitive.

Toxoids: The Malons start with the relentless industrialists civic.
STH_qpedia.1.g.response:
Available to: United Federation of Planets, Klingon Empire, The Dominion & Romulans. 

The science station, known in lore as Jupiter Station is a unique Federation megastructure that provides access to unique research options and scientist leaders. It is buildable once you have unlocked Advanced Scientific Method and must be built via a constructor from the megastructure build menu over a gas giant.

Once built you can contact the science department either via the main contacts menu or by clicking on the science station's country flag icon (the same way you would contact another empire). From here you can view the unique techs that are researchable, unique leaders, and if you are playing the Federation the Member World's unique technologies. 
Dev Note: Ship-of-the-line techs can be unlocked via the unique tech research option.
STH_qpedia.1.kdf.response: Qapla', headbutt and all that Klingony stuff... yes yes honour blah blah...come this way for more info...
STH_qpedia.1.name: The Q Continuum
STH_qpedia.1.pre.response:
Missing the good-old Jean-Luc are we? Well no worries. By using the Pre-TNG start you will be transported straight to year 2300 and so are much much closer to your hero. Here is what you need to know about it: 

To get the proper start date in 2300 you need to have the ST:NH TNG Era Start submod on. As without it the start date will be 2150. 

For the Pre-TNG and Pre-TNG-Mirror starts only use maps that have those Pre-TNG and Pre-TNG-Mirror words in their title. If you want to play as the Federation on the Pre-TNG maps select the empire United Federation of Planets (2300s), do not use the regular United Earth or the other 2150 Federation founding empires. 

For Pre-TNG mirror maps use the empire Terran Rebelion (2300s) if you want to play as humans, the United Federation of Planets does not exist here. Other unique selections for these maps are the Klingon-Cardassian alliance (2300s) and Republic of Hope (2300s).
STH_qpedia.1.ufp.response: Ahh yes.... Picard said you might be interested in this one. Come this way for all the info you could want on everyone's favorite goody-goodies!
STH_qpedia.10.c.response: As of our 3.6 update, you can now talk to the Federation Council and access some unique mechanics via the UFP Council.
STH_qpedia.10.c: Can I talk to the council at any time?
STH_qpedia.10.d.response:
The Federation will form via an event that spawns after 15 in-game years if you meet the following conditions... You are playing as one of the 4 Federation Founders (Earth, Vulcan, Tellar or the Andorians) and are in an alliance with at least 3 of those empires. All of these empires must be at peace with no ongoing crisis, such as the Vulcan civil war, Demons, or Xindi Events.

An event called the Babel Conference can also take place to help if the Founders are on bad terms with each other!
STH_qpedia.10.d: How do I form the Federation?
STH_qpedia.10.desc:
I had a bet with my good pal Jean-Luc about how long it would take for a question on his precious Federation of Planets would take to come in .

The UFP has some of the mods most exciting and oldest mechanics and once you get used to them you'll be Federating the galaxy in no time, just like the Borg... but with a nicer smile!
STH_qpedia.10.e.response:
Ships of the Line is a unique tradition tree for the UFP (which will eventually come to more empires), it grants access to options for extra ships outside of the core fleet. These ships may offer unique perks, or simply a new aesthetic and are selected from canon and some non-canon choices that the Devs just really like.

Each branch unlocks when you reach the ingame era corresponding to the group of ships (ENT, DIS, TOS, TMP, TNG/TNG+) once unlocked you can make the research available via the Science Station Menu it will then be researchable as an option via the research menu. Certain refit designs require the original ship to be available before it can be used (such as the Spokane refit for the Curry Class, or the Vigilant refit for the Defiant) and the designs will not appear in the Science Station research menu until you enter the correct time period to avoid issues with outfitting them with the correct tech. 

Once all branches of this tree are unlocked a unique accession perk is available with some very special end-game ships! 

Dev Note: These ships are entirely optional and are there to add some extra flavour to the game, this means they are not strictly aligned with the core fleet.
STH_qpedia.10.f.response:
What would a Star Trek game be without the Enterprise? 

These very special ships are buildable from the Utopia Planitia shipyards Megastructure, and lets you add the NCC-1701 - NCC-1701-F into your game. Each new version of the Enterprise unlocks as you unlock the tech that also unlocks the regular version of the class and a nice pop-up should let you know when a new design is available. 

Flagships come in two options Science Version or Military Version (except the Ent-F which is only available as a Military Flagship). 
The Science Version is a unique science ship, which means it can survey systems, but also comes equipped with impressive firepower. As with all science vessels, they cannot join fleets and require a scientist to lead them.
MIlitary Flagships are very powerful, but regular warships, come with special modifiers that make them deadly in combat. 

Be careful though, using these ships comes with a risk, should your flagship be destroyed you must wait until the next class version is available... no do-overs here! 

In order to build the next version of the Enterprise, make sure the tech is available and the class exists in the ship designer, and you no longer have the older version active in your fleet (except the NX-01, this ship does not count as part of the 1701 family ... you can keep it!).
STH_qpedia.10.g.response: Buildable from Utopia Planitia Megastructure these ships represent some of the more famous ships in Star Trek lore, they are formidable ships and add a bit of extra Trek flavour to the game! Some even come with unique missions... watch out for those badlands USS Voyager!
STH_qpedia.10.name: The Humans
STH_qpedia.100.c.response: The Borg fleets in battle will slowly adapt to the weapons they face reducing the damage enemy weapons inflict upon them until finally when fully adapted taking no damage from them at all. When Borg fleets are not in battle this adaptation level drops slowly. The enemies of the Borg can use special anti-Borg edicts such as Anti-Borg Frequency Remodulators or Anti-Borg Tactical Innovations to either slow down this adaption or reduce the time Borg stay adapted against their weapons. On the other hand the Borg also have a tradition tree called Adaptability that gives them bonuses to various aspects of adaptation.
STH_qpedia.100.d.response: To unlock the Colony harvest espionage operation you need to first adopt the Harvesting tradition tree which then makes it possible to harvest colonies from 1 pop to 15 pops. And once you have done the Hyper-Compression Patter buffers tradition the limit rises to colonies from 1 to 30 pops. However you cannot harvest anyone's homeworld or Undine colonies. Also no war or truce is allowed with the target empire when trying to harvest.
STH_qpedia.100.desc: Perfection. So close yet still so very very far for you. Take it from someone who knows. Now with what knowledge would you wish to improve yourself today?
STH_qpedia.100.e.response: Transwarp conduits allow ships to move between two built conduit entries (Transwarp conduit megastructures) at a very rapid rate. Initially these conduits are only available for Borg fleets to enter, but fighting against the Borg may yield the technology for other empires to also take advantage of them. The Transwarp Aparture Hub functions like regular Stellaris Quantum Catapult megastructure moving your fleet close to the set destination within the catapults range. To use the Aparture you need to have a fleet in the same system as it and then choose the Catapult-fleet option from the fleet UI.
STH_qpedia.100.e: Transwarp conduit and Transwarp Aperture Hub.
STH_qpedia.100.name: The Borg Collective
STH_qpedia.11.a: What or Where is Starbase One?
STH_qpedia.11.b: What can I do with the Council?
STH_qpedia.11.desc: As of our 3.6 update, you can summon the UFP council to Starbase one for a meeting to discuss key events and help manage the Federation and its member worlds. Some worlds will appreciate the support, while others might become frustrated with the micro-management. To open this mechanic simply click on the UFP emblem next to Starbase one or contact them via the contacts tab.
STH_qpedia.11.name: Starbase One
STH_qpedia.1111.a.response: Arguing with the Q, well, well... that's a risky decision, whole fleets have been known to vanish in a.... snap.
STH_qpedia.1111.name: Locked out system [From.GetName].
STH_qpedia.1112.desc:
Dev Note: As part of our 4.0 release, we have examined several performance improvements and decided that we need to modify how the decision techs operate. These techs, once researched, enable you to select from multiple specialisations. 

In the 4.0 update, these will now be checked every 3 months, which will cause a small delay between the research being completed and the decision being made. 

If you would like to force the event to run earlier, then run STH_custom.51 from the console.
STH_qpedia.1112.name: Decision Techs
STH_qpedia.12.desc:
You may have noticed that an extra pop-up appeared after you formed the Federation, well that formed the council, as well as giving you lots of planets, leaders, and cool new ships.

If you look over Neptune in the Sol system or one of your gas giants if you are not playing as Earth you will see a new megastructure that resembles Starbase One, as seen in Discovery and Strange New Worlds... click on it, just like you would click on another countries ships to talk to them.
STH_qpedia.12.name: Starbase One
STH_qpedia.13.a.response: This gives you the most options and allows you to directly update your member's home systems. From here you can fund a starbase upgrade (if you have the tech), you can transfer some of your ships to them or seek there advice on winning a war.
STH_qpedia.13.b.response: You can select which era of Federation Flag you wish to represent the UFP.
STH_qpedia.13.desc: Now that the Council has assembled you have a number of options to manage your members and run the Federation as you wish.
STH_qpedia.13.name: The Federation Council
STH_qpedia.2.desc:
The Q Continuum is bursting with knowledge and has introduced a new means of helping players play the many unique features of ST:New Horizons. 

The Q-pedia contains the collective knowledge of the Q with handy questions on how certain mechanics work and is worth a peak if you get stuck! 

If you need to open the help section, contact Q from the Contacts tab and there via Adv Diplomacy which now not only allows you to change the starting conditions but also find these helpful articles.
STH_qpedia.2.name: Q-pedia
STH_qpedia.200.a.response: To escape fluidic space you need to either complete the events in 'Masters of Fluidic Space' event chain and wait for the Borg to show up or make use of the edict 'Unleash the Vanguard' which comes available after 20 years.
STH_qpedia.200.a: How do I get out of fluidic space?
STH_qpedia.200.b.response: Building a Holding Pen on each Fluidic realm planet will allow non fluidic species to be placed on those planets without getting purged.
STH_qpedia.200.b: How can I avoid purging none fluidic pops?
STH_qpedia.200.c.response: In order to become the crisis as Undine you need to have the Nemesis DLC on and attack the main galaxy during the event 'The Purge' as the Undine Infesters.
STH_qpedia.200.c: How to become the crisis as Undine?
STH_qpedia.200.desc: Oh the Undine with their famous motto, 'the weak shall perish.' Such hostile creatures to visitors in their space. But if you are going to keep up with that attitude there might be some useful things for you to know.
STH_qpedia.200.name: The Undine
STH_qpedia.300.a.response:
As you may have noticed the Dominion has 3 different types of basic pops. The Founders also known as shape-shifters are the rulers of the Dominion. Considered as gods by the Vorta and Jem'Hadar the Founders mainly handle the most prestigious jobs in the Dominion. 

The Vorta act as commanders, administrators, scientists and diplomats for the Founders, utterly loyal to their will.

The military arm of the Dominion is run by the Jem'Hadar, a genetically engineered race who are birthed and genetically modified to be perfect soldiers. Their loyalty is guaranteed by a drug called ketracel-white, which is their sole source of food and nourishment.
STH_qpedia.300.a: The Founder, Vorta and Jem'Hadar pops.
STH_qpedia.300.b.response:
Ketracel-White is a special resource that provides sustenance to your Jem'Hadar pops. It is also a way the Dominion rulers, the Founders, ensure the loyalty of the fierce Jem'Hadar warriors. 

Ketracel-White can be produced in two ways. Either find a planet that you can build a Ketracel-White Refinery on or once you have researched the technology build a Synthetic Ketracel-White Refinery on a planet. Alternatively you can also look to buy some Ketracel-White from the Market.
STH_qpedia.300.c.response:
A Dominion Member World is a special type of vassal for the Dominion. This vassal type will offer you some of its resources as well as a unique vassal specialization tree that offers new benefits after each level on the tree is reached. You can view this tree and the vassal in-general from Contacts and there Agreements. It can even help you defend the Dominion. 

But can I get more of these vassals, I hear you asking? Sure just select Expand the Dominion war goal when you declare war to your neighbour.
STH_qpedia.300.c: What is a Dominion Member World?
STH_qpedia.300.desc: Ah the Dominion, a bunch of shape-shifters who can do cute little form tricks while playing as gods for those species that cannot. How cute. What do you want to know about them?
STH_qpedia.300.name: The Dominion
STH_qpedia.50.desc: Well glory to you and to your tiny house and all that other Klingon nonsense. What do you wish to know more about?
STH_qpedia.50.name: The Klingon Empire
STH_qpedia.70.b.response: Not every empire has the audacity to impose its ideals on other empires, pacifists in particular (and this included the Federation) like to think they are above such things. But I want to... I hear you shout, well you can all you need is the Righteous minds tradition in the Force of Will Then, ensure you have changed your war policy to include ideological wars and you can go on your merry way pushing your views on anyone who will listen and now those that don't.
STH_qpedia.70.b: Why can't I impose my ideology?
STH_qpedia.70.desc: War... what is it good for? Well as it turns out, it's good for rather a lot. Whether you want to take some territory, defend yourself, or those many human words you have just don't seem as much fun as firing a torpedo at a helpless hull. Here you can find enough bits of info on war to make Sun Tzu want to write a second book.
STH_qpedia.70.name: War! What is it good for?
STH_qpedia.71.a.response: With enough influence you can claim another empires systems and declare war to win ownership of said system.
STH_qpedia.71.b.response: Can be declared by all normal countries with unrestricted wars or ideological wars policy. Forces an empire that you have tried to subjugate diplomatically to become your subject. When playing as the Dominion victory forces them to become Dominion Member states.
STH_qpedia.71.c.response: Forces your ideology onto another empire, can be used by all normal countries with has unrestricted wars or ideological wars policy and not gestalt consciousness. Cannot be declared on an empire with the same ideology as you... for obvious reasons.
STH_qpedia.71.d.response: May only be used by a barbaric society or one with the barbaric despoilers civic.
STH_qpedia.71.desc: This section of the Q-pedia list the requirement for each Casus Belli in STNH.
STH_qpedia.71.e.response: The Borg can declare their intent to assimilate their neighbours, victory forces the loser to submit to the Borg, who will eventually assimilate their culture and make them adapt to service the Collective. The AI Borg will operate a sleep cycle and will often ignore empires that are less technologically advance than themselves.
STH_qpedia.71.f.response: Any neighbour of the Borg or allied empire who neighbours the Borg may declare a defensive war on the Collective. Also you can declare war on the Borg if they have used their colony scoop against you... those devious cyborgs.
STH_qpedia.71.g.response: You can declare war on any target that is at war with any of your allies, countries you are guaranteeing or associate empires.
STH_qpedia.71.name: How do Casus Belli Work?
STH_qpedia.90.desc: Ah the Romulans, always scheming and plotting something in secrecy aren't you? Well as it turns out I know all of your petty little secrets, so just ask away.
STH_qpedia.90.name: The Romulan Star Empire
STH_redemption.10.desc: Ambassador K'Ehleyr from the Federation has confirmed that the Federation is sending one of their warriors to meet with us to discuss the Rite of Succession, and whilst they proclaim they will not directly interfere they will hear our ask.
STH_redemption.10.name: Rite of Succession
STH_redemption.11.desc: Our failure to attend our own conference has no doubt led to confusion within our own ranks and frustration within the decks of the Starfleet vessel that was waiting to rendezvous with us.
STH_redemption.11.name: Rite of Succession
STH_redemption.12.desc: The Klingons have never been known as a patient people and our failure to attend the agreed meeting has nothing to improve relations and will have harmed our efforts to build a peaceful quadrant.
STH_redemption.12.name: Rite of Succession
STH_redemption.13.desc: It appears the Klingons have failed to attend the arranged meeting with the Federation Flagship, a baffling and cowardly act from the Klingons, however one can never fathom the actions of such a foolish species. It does however. put an end to our schemes in this area.
STH_redemption.13.name: Klingons Fail to Attend
STH_redemption.14.desc: The Federation has demonstrated a lack of honour by failing to attend the agreed meeting, perhaps we have miss-judged them.
STH_redemption.14.name: Rite of Succession
STH_redemption.15.desc: The Klingons have never been known as a patient people and our failure to attend the agreed meeting has nothing to improve relations and will have harmed our efforts to build a peaceful quadrant.
STH_redemption.15.name: Rite of Succession
STH_redemption.16.desc: It appears the Federation have failed to attend the arranged meeting with the Klingon Flagship, a rather baffling and cowardly act from Starfleet, which puts an end to our schemes in this area.
STH_redemption.16.name: Federation fail to Attend
STH_redemption.17.a: Let the Rite of Succession begin.
STH_redemption.17.desc: Commander [klingon_redemption_1_leader.GetName] has successfully delivered Chancellor [klingon_leader.GetName] to their meeting with the Federation Flagship, now begins a hazardous situation for the Klingon Empire as a new ruler must be selected to guide them Empire through this new era.
STH_redemption.17.name: Redemption
STH_redemption.18.a: You had better be correct Sela.
